title: Income tax reassessment - the time limits after recent legal changes
p1:
Think the tax department can reopen old assessments anytime? Many taxpayers still believe that a notice can arrive years later without limits.

That is not the case. Recent changes have reshaped the rules around how far back an income tax reassessment can go.
p2:
A common misconception is that any past return can be questioned indefinitely. In reality, the law sets specific time limits depending on the situation and the value of income that may have escaped assessment.

The surprising part? For many cases, the window for reopening older years is now much shorter than what people assume.
p3:
In simple terms, reassessment means the tax department reviewing a completed assessment again if it believes some income was missed earlier. But this power comes with boundaries. The exact period depends on factors like the assessment year and the nature of the information available.

For taxpayers and businesses, keeping records and responding within timelines is critical. A notice should never be ignored just because it relates to an older year.
conclusion: Did you know that income tax reassessment has strict time limits? Do you think taxpayers are generally aware of these deadlines?
